Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neal (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM), Dr. Elena Ruiz (Silverpine), Marcus Li (Silverpine), Aisha Brown (Silverpine PM), Kevin O'Donnell (Silverpine Sec), Sofia Park (Silverpine MLOps)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about an hour so we'll try to be tight. i'm maya from redwood, i'll be your AE, with liam our se and priya who will run the onboarding.
[00:17] Elena: thanks maya, appreciate it. we want to make sure this pilot maps to our regulated pipeline, so security first, then perf.
[00:25] Maya: totally understood. quick roll call and then we'll hand to liam to go through the playbook.
[00:33] Marcus: quick note, we only allow service endpoints into our staging VPC, no public endpoints.
[00:40] Liam: ok, that's fine, we support VPC peering and private deployment models. small caveat: the private package has a slightly different control plane, but functionally same API.
[00:52] Kevin: how does key management work? we need HSM-backed KMS and proof of key rotation logs.
[00:59] Liam: yes, we integrate with customer KMSs and HSMs via our private deployment, and we stream audit events to your SIEM. sometimes the transcript here misreads, but we'll attach the SOC2 matrix.
[01:12] Priya: i'll be owning the weekly syncs and the project plan, quick note, we'll do a 6-week pilot with milestones at week 2 (staging integration), week 4 (canary traffic), week 6 (pilot review + expansion decision).
[01:28] Aisha: that timeline works. success metrics — target p95 latency <200ms for our chat routing, and cost per token benchmark to be under $0.003 average.
[01:41] Liam: p95 sub-200 is reasonable depending on model and sequence lengths; we'll run benchmarks. for cost targets, we can recommend quantized variants and batching to hit that number.
[01:55] Elena: we're using a mixture of long context logs and short prompts, so kv-cache behavior is important. how does redwood handle prefix caching?
[02:07] Liam: we have KV caching and prefix cache; depends on model and runtime. note: sometimes docs call it KV cache or key-v cache in transcriptions. we'll map your prompt patterns and suggest TTLs, and caching will live either in the host or within your private runtime depending on deployment.
[02:30] Marcus: network details: we'll need a terraform example for the peering, and an IP allowlist. can you provide those?
[02:38] Maya: yes, we'll share a terraform snippet and a runbook link after this call. link: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/silverpine (placeholder).
[02:49] Kevin: audit logs retention — we need 2 years. can redwood support that?
[02:55] Liam: built-in retention can be extended on Private; for Hosted/Dedicated we'd need an add-on. we'll include options in the runbook.
[03:08] Elena: about model versions — we need model pinning for reproducibility in our trials. is that supported?
[03:14] Liam: yes, you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts. also we support automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency spikes, that's part of our graceful degradation story.
[03:28] Aisha: who do we contact during the pilot for urgent issues?
[03:32] Priya: i'll be primary, but liam will be the escalation engineering contact. maya handles commercial but will surface blockers.
[03:40] Marcus: small question about network egress costs, do you see additional charges from redwood side?
[03:46] Maya: depends on deployment. Dedicated has predictable capacity pricing; Private typically has infra cost on the customer's side. we'll detail these in the pricing appendix.
[03:58] Elena: can we run an initial small perf test this week to sanity check latency numbers?
[04:03] Liam: yes, we'll provide a lightweight script — it will be synthetic but will surface major config issues.
[04:12] Sofia: on quantization, we have custom ops; we need to know what kernels are used, especially for our A100 fleet.
[04:20] Liam: we'll show recommended kernels and quantization profiles in the deep dive. note that kernel selection sometimes varies by runtime and model — we'll capture that in the runbook.
[04:33] Kevin: also need to validate SSO/SAML integrations and RBAC for developer accounts.
[04:39] Priya: yes, we have a standard SAML guide. initial access will use token-scoped accounts and then we'll map SSO groups.
[04:47] Elena: what about data residency? our patient PII must remain in eu-west-1 region.
[04:52] Maya: we can pin regions for deployments. if hosted is not acceptable we will propose Private in your region, or Dedicated in eu-west if available.
[05:05] Marcus: ok next, can we define the pilot success criteria again briefly?
[05:10] Priya: sure — criteria: 1) integration completed into staging, 2) perf targets met (p95 latency <200ms), 3) cost target under $0.003 per token (or comparable metric for embeddings), 4) no critical security gaps per Kevin's list.
[05:25] Elena: plus a manual quality eval for outputs on our prompt set — we will provide a 50-prompt eval.
[05:31] Liam: perfect — we'll run automated evals and then a human review. we'll version the prompts so we can detect regressions.
[05:45] Aisha: how do we do rollbacks if a model update causes regressions?
[05:50] Liam: we support immediate pin + rollback via canary controls and an automatic fallback policy. will document the steps in the runbook.
[06:03] Kevin: please enumerate compliance artifacts: SOC2 cert, pen test, infra diagram, data flow.
[06:10] Maya: we'll attach the SOC2 package and a pen test summary. note some names in the auto-transcript are funky but the attachments will be clean.
[06:20] Elena: for the pilot, we prefer not to ingest any raw PII into hosted logs; can we have log redaction?
[06:28] Liam: yes, we can redact at the SDK level and mask tokens in logs. for extra assurance, Private keeps logs local to your environment.
[06:36] Marcus: timeline clarification: who signs off at week 6?
[06:40] Priya: Elena and Kevin will own sign-off for quality and security respectively; Aisha will sign for product acceptance.
[06:50] Maya: ok i'll recap next steps at the end, but a couple of logistics: i'll send the runbook and terraform examples, liam will publish the perf script, priya will set the weekly cadence.
[07:02] Aisha: sounds good. one more question about telemetry — can we get token-level cost breakdowns per route?
[07:09] Liam: yes, our console can break down per-route token usage and cost, and we can expose that via API too.
[07:18] Kevin: last sec on legal — we'll need a DP addendum for EU data flows. legal will reach out.
[07:24] Maya: ok we will loop legal in the thread.
[07:30] --- mid-call technical aside ---
[07:35] Liam: small note on caching — if you have many short prompts we will favor prefix caching and aggressive batching; for long context we may favor KV-cache persistence. mixing patterns we will tune TTLs.
[07:50] Sofia: we'll send sample prompt distributions and a couple of long chat transcripts to help tuning.
[07:57] Liam: perfect, that will help a lot.
[08:05] Elena: question on monitoring — do you expose event traces to our tracing system?
[08:11] Liam: yes, we have tracing hooks and can forward spans to your jaeger/newrelic; we'll document the tracing headers.
[08:20] Marcus: earlier you mentioned fallback to cheaper variant — how do we ensure quality doesn't drop below threshold?
[08:27] Liam: fallback policies can be coupled with quality gate checks — e.g., automatic fallback triggers only if latency breach, but if you want output-quality gating we can require a manual approval or a soft fallback with sampling.
[08:42] Priya: okay team, we are at 40 minutes in, let's capture open items.
[08:48] Maya: action items: i'll send runbook and pricing appendix; liam will send perf script; kevin will send security Qs; marcus will share VPC details; priya will schedule weekly syncs.
[09:00] Elena: great. one clarification — do we lock a model for the canary or will redwood push updates?
[09:07] Liam: you control model rollouts and pins, redwood will not push breaking updates without a rollout plan.
[09:16] Aisha: ok thanks.
[09:20] Maya: all right, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the runbook and a calendar invite for the quantization deep dive.
